arguments.text: `parseDigits` returns `NaN` when the input contains no parseable digits (e.g. `parseDigits("abc")`). It first tries `parseInt(str, 10)`, which is `NaN`; it then scans each character for Han decimal or other numbering-system digit ranges, accumulates nothing (leaving the accumulator as the empty string `""`), and finally returns `parseInt("", 10)`, which is `NaN`.

arguments.text: When the input doesn't match the regex, `match` returns the two-element array `[null, {}]`: the first element is the failed `String.prototype.match` result (`null`), and the second is an empty object of parsed values. Callers check the first element for truthiness (e.g. `if (matches)`), so `null` signals "no match" while the empty object means "no tokens extracted".

arguments.text: When `matches.Z` is defined, `dateTimeFromMatches` sets the zone to `new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` — i.e. a fixed-offset zone built from the parsed offset value (the `Z` token's deserializer already converted the offset text into minutes). That zone is returned as the second element of the `[vals, zone]` pair. (For comparison: if `Z` is undefined but `matches.z` is defined it uses `IANAZone.create(matches.z)`, otherwise `zone` is `null`.)

arguments.text: Hour 24 is valid only when the rest of the time is exactly zero: `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) || (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0)`. So `24:00:00.000` is accepted (the ISO end-of-day representation), while e.g. `24:00:00.001` or `24:30` is rejected with a `unit out of range` invalid for the hour.
`Zone#formatOffset(ts, format)` accepts three formats: `'narrow'` (e.g. `+6`), `'short'` (e.g. `+06:00`) and `'techie'` (e.g. `+0600`), as documented in its docstring.

Fixed and verified: `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` now pads negative numbers correctly (e.g. year -5 renders as `-0005`, not `00-5`), so `DateTime#toISODate()` pads negative years properly. Full suite still green apart from the two pre-existing locale failures.

Fixed and verified: `objToLocalTS` in `src/impl/util.js` now re-sets the year via `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` instead of subtracting 1900 from the normalized year, so day overflow is re-normalized in the real (proleptic Gregorian) year. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({days: 61})` now gives 0100-03-02 (was 0100-03-01, off by one because 2000 is a leap year but 100 is not). A brute-force check of 100+ day offsets across the 100 barrier through February now matches the reference calendar exactly, and the suite is green.

Fixed and verified: `casualMatrix`/`accurateMatrix` in `src/duration.js` were missing the `years.quarters` (4) and `quarters.seconds` (91*24*60*60) entries, so `Duration#normalize` produced NaN for the years↔quarters and quarters↔seconds unit pairs. All 72 unit pairs now normalize correctly for both `casual` and `longterm` accuracy, and the existing normalize tests still pass.

Fixed and verified: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)` instead of always `true`, so `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` is invalid and a DateTime in such a zone is itself invalid with reason "unsupported zone". Existing fixed-offset zone tests still pass.

arguments.text: Fixed and verified: `isInDST` now compares the current offset against the offsets of January 1st and May 1st of the same year (`set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` / `set({ month: 5, day: 1 })`) instead of dates that kept the current day-of-month. Previously, for 1974 in the USA (DST ran Jan 6 – Oct 27) any date from Jan 6 on had its January counterpart also in DST, so `isInDST` was false for the entire year; now the whole Jan 6 – Oct 27 window reports true and the rest false (verified day-by-day for all of 1974 in America/New_York). The existing isInDST tests (pre/during/post-DST, UTC/fixed offsets, invalid) all still pass, and the full suite shows only the two pre-existing locale failures.
